analysis.title: Retail at Thanksgiving
key_insights: NRF forecasts Nov-Dec 2026 US retail sales at a record $1.013tn, up 4.2% versus 3.1% growth in 2025. After inflation, roughly half of the projected increase is real growth.
Real disposable income fell 0.3% month-on-month in September, real consumption was broadly flat and the saving rate declined to 3.8%. Households have less room to absorb price or employment shocks.
Pictet treats resilient holiday demand as the base case rather than a catalyst. The case is stronger for selectivity within Retail than for broad sector exposure into the holiday season.

Historically the equal-weighted Retail index outperforms the broader market ahead of Thanksgiving, then loses momentum. Average relative performance troughs near -2.3% by end of January, and the share of positive observations stays below 50% across much of the post-Thanksgiving period.

Consumer confidence is subdued with diverging signals. The Conference Board Expectations Index rose to 72.6 in October from 65.7 in September. Michigan sentiment fell for three consecutive months to 48.0 in October from 55.2 in July.

The XRT/S&P 500 equal-weight ratio rebounded from a September low of 0.387 to about 0.420 in early November, then slipped to 0.409 by 17 November. Pictet reads this as improving relative momentum, not a trend reversal.
The 14-day RSI on Retail rose from below 40 in September to about 70 in early November, then fell back to 48.2 by 17 November, which is neutral territory.

Leadership within Retail has fragmented. Mid-Market gained 35.6% over six months and Discount Retail 28.8%. Premium Value is up 15.5% over three months versus 10.2% for Mid-Market. Off-Price fell 16.6% over three months and 9.1% over six months, 44.7 percentage points behind Mid-Market over six months.

In the S&P Retail Select Industry, 56% of reporting companies beat expectations and 55% had a positive price reaction, while the aggregate earnings surprise is -2.1%. Consumer Staples Distribution & Retail has +7.7% blended earnings growth and an +8.3% aggregate surprise, but only 38% of companies had a positive price reaction. Specialty Retail has +7.7% earnings growth, +2.8% surprises and 58% positive reactions.

With 42 of 74 companies reported, blended Q3 EPS growth for the S&P Retail Select Industry is 2.4%. Carvana (+97.7%), Target (+48.8%) and Costco (+15.0%) are strongest. Coupang (-649.7%) and Tractor Supply (-13.7%) declined.

With 57% of companies reported, blended Q3 sales growth is 7.9% (10.0% for those already reported), led by Carvana (+42.4%), Murphy USA (+34.8%) and CarMax (+19.5%). Amazon (+12.1%) and Costco (+11.1%) also grew double digits. Sales are not converting evenly into earnings, which puts focus on margins.

The Earnings Revision Ratio peaked near 42% in June and fell from 21.7% in early October to -7.0% by 13 November, so downward revisions now outnumber upward ones. The sector's 1-year return recovered from -5.0% in early October to +13.8% by mid-November, so price has run ahead of revisions.

XRT remains in a medium-term uptrend, above its rising 50-day SMA (86.14) and 200-day SMA (85.71). The rally stalled near the 76.4% Fibonacci retracement at 93.33, with rejection below 94.93 marking a third failed test of that resistance.

XRT support zone is 88.29-85.71. A pullback that holds it and forms a higher low would reinforce the uptrend. A sustained break below the 200-day SMA would bring 81.65 into focus. A confirmed break above 94.93 targets 104.89 as the next major resistance.

TJX, Ross Stores and Burlington have all sold off. Ross shows a divergence between earnings revisions and share price. TJX combines a significant derating with positive estimates. Burlington's deeper sell-off is less clear-cut and depends on coming earnings, margins and guidance.

Pictet screened US Retail for a Global grade of at least 50, a 3M price change below 10% and positive 3M EPS revisions, to find names where price has lagged improving earnings expectations. The screen results table is not in the text.

market_movers.rationale: Pictet flags a notable divergence between Ross's earnings revisions and its share-price performance after the Off-Price sell-off. This is a screen observation, not a rating.
TJX combines a significant derating with positive estimates, per Pictet. This is a screen observation, not a rating.
Burlington's deeper sell-off gives a less clear-cut picture, and Pictet puts more weight on subsequent earnings, margins and guidance.

sector_views.rationale: Holiday demand is expected to be resilient but is already the base case. Pictet favors selectivity over broad sector exposure, with weak revisions and cooled momentum against a still-intact medium-term uptrend.
Off-Price is the clearest dislocation, down 16.6% over three months. Pictet asks whether this is deteriorating fundamentals or an expectations reset and gives no verdict.

earnings_insights: S&P Retail Select Industry Q3 blended EPS growth is 2.4% with 42 of 74 companies reported (actual reported figures, FactSet as of 18/11/2026). The aggregate earnings surprise is -2.1%, and 56% of reporters beat expectations.
Q3 blended sales growth is 7.9% with 57% of companies reported, versus 10.0% for those that have already reported (reported figures, FactSet).

Reported Q3 EPS growth: Carvana +97.7%, Target +48.8%, Costco +15.0%, Coupang -649.7%, Tractor Supply -13.7%. Reported Q3 sales growth: Carvana +42.4%, Murphy USA +34.8%, CarMax +19.5%, Amazon +12.1%, Costco +11.1%.

Consumer Staples Distribution & Retail reported +7.7% blended earnings growth and an +8.3% aggregate surprise, with 57% beating but only 38% seeing a positive price reaction. Specialty Retail reported +7.7% growth and +2.8% surprises, with 58% seeing positive reactions.
The Earnings Revision Ratio was -7.0% on 13 November, down from 21.7% in early October and about 42% in June. Downward estimate revisions now outnumber upward ones.

macro_indicators.interpretation: A record nominal total, but roughly half of the growth is inflation. Underlying demand is supportive but softer than the headline.
The comparison base for the 2026 forecast of +4.2%.
Falling real income reduces the consumer cushion going into the holidays.
A lower saving rate leaves households less room to absorb price or job shocks.
Rebounded but broadly range-bound through 2026 and well below late-2024 levels.
Down three consecutive months, showing weaker household finances and buying conditions.

risk_factors: Thinning consumer cushion: falling real disposable income, a saving rate of 3.8% and sensitivity to prices, promotions and employment.
Sensitivity to inflation and rising borrowing costs, with employment and income trends key for consumption.
Earnings revisions are deteriorating while prices have rallied.
A sustained break below the XRT 200-day SMA (85.71) would weaken the recovery and bring 81.65 into focus.
Off-Price weakness may reflect deteriorating fundamentals in comps, transaction growth, merchandise margins and guidance.
Sales strength is not converting evenly into earnings, so margins and operating leverage are the risk.
vol_and_positioning: The 14-day RSI on US Retail fell from about 70 in early November (briefly overbought) to 48.2 on 17 November, which is neutral and not oversold.
The Earnings Revision Ratio of -7.0% against a +13.8% 1-year sector return shows price running ahead of estimate revisions.
Historically the Retail index gains relative to the market before Thanksgiving, then underperforms, with a trough of about -2.3% by end of January.

tension_points.bull_case: XRT remains in a medium-term uptrend above its rising 50-day and 200-day SMAs, record holiday sales are expected, and the September lows have held.
tension_points.bear_case: Earnings revisions have turned negative (-7.0% ERR) while the 1-year return rose to +13.8%. Momentum has cooled, the 94.93 resistance has failed three times, and Retail has historically lost momentum after Thanksgiving.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sustained break below the XRT 200-day SMA at 85.71 would weaken the recovery and bring 81.65 into focus.

tension_points.bull_case: The weakness may be an expectations reset, with TJX showing positive estimates alongside a significant derating and Ross showing a divergence between revisions and price.
tension_points.bear_case: The weakness may reflect deteriorating fundamentals in comps, transaction growth, merchandise margins and guidance, and Burlington's deeper sell-off is less clear-cut.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Subsequent earnings, margins and guidance from TJX, Ross and Burlington would show whether fundamentals support a stabilisation.
